root_cause_measured_2026_09_13_2345: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (builder cron af3e62239ce2, worktree /home/jericho/projects/zion/worktrees/d26-probe @ clean HEAD 91820ce): the flake is PYTHONHASHSEED dependence, not sweep contention. src/pixel_embeddings.py:94 hashes char n-grams into feature indices with plain hash(ngram) % feature_dim; Python randomizes str hash per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the feature matrix itself differs per run. The assertion in test_pixel_embeddings_neighbors (tests/test_pixel_embeddings.py:110, "embed_optical in neighbors of embed_visual, k=3") is seed-sensitive: at seeds 6/8/12 the k=3 neighborhood omits embed_optical and the test FAILS; at seeds 0-5,7,9-11 it PASSES (3/13 pinned seeds red in one scan; 12/12 greens on other seeds across repeat runs). Isolation-only greens (both prior baseline readings) were lucky seeds; the sweep-context FAIL was an unlucky seed - per-worker processes draw fresh random seeds, so -w 4 vs -w 1 changes exposure but ANY run can hit it. Reproduced end-to-end through real pytest at clean HEAD, no env, no contention: PYTHONHASHSEED=6/8/12 pytest tests/test_pixel_embeddings.py -q -> "1 failed, 5 passed" reproducibly; seeds 0/1/2 -> "6 passed". Artifacts: output/d26_probe_summary.txt, output/d26_probe2_seedscan.txt (in the d26-probe worktree), probes .builder_queue/probe_d26_hashseed.py / probe_d26_hashseed2.py. NOTE: the seed scan measures sensitivity of ONE assertion at n=13 seeds; the per-seed red rate over the full seed space is NOT established (mechanism is proven; a full-sweep seed census is overkill).
